clean-rs.py.summary: Strip the comments from Rust files while keeping the doc and ``SAFETY:`` comments.
details: Parses each ``.rs`` file with tree-sitter, removes the line and block comments except the ``///``/``//!`` documentation and the ``SAFETY:`` notes, collapses the resulting blank-line runs, validates the output and offers ``-diff`` for a coloured preview.

clean_version.py.summary: Reduce a ``pip freeze`` file to the bare package names.
details: Drops the version pins, the comments, the URLs and the VCS requirements, deduplicates what is left and overwrites the file with one name per line.

cleanbash.py.summary: Remove the comments from bash scripts with tree-sitter.
details: Detects the shell scripts by suffix and shebang, deletes the comment nodes, collapses the excess blank lines, re-validates the script with ``bash -n`` and processes the tree with a spawn-based pool.

cleanlua.py.summary: Remove the comments from Lua files, keeping the ``---`` annotations.
details: Collects the comment ranges with tree-sitter Lua, preserves the three-dash documentation comments, rewrites the files and works through the tree in a pool.

cleanmd.py.summary: Remove the image references from Markdown, RST and HTML files.
details: Deletes the inline images, the reference-style images and the linked badges (``--badges``), optionally only the remote ones, the unused link definitions and the surrounding whitespace; ``--backup``, ``--html-parser`` and ``--report`` control the behaviour.

cleanpy.py.summary: Remove the comments and docstrings of Python files recursively.
details: Uses LibCST to delete the comments and the class/function docstrings while preserving the shebangs, the ``# fmt``/``# type`` markers and the module docstrings (``-r`` removes those too), and processes the tree with eight workers.

cleants.py.summary: Strip the comments from source files of many languages with tree-sitter.
details: Detects the language from the suffix or shebang (bash, C/C++, Python, JS/TS, CSS ...), keeps the vital comments (licences, ``@license``, lint pragmas) and the doc blocks (``--keep-doc``), and offers ``--inplace``, ``--dryrun``, ``--check``, ``--diff``, ``--backup``, ``--exclude`` and a size limit, validating every result before writing.

colortools.py.summary: Colour utilities: extract, convert, sort and display hex colours.
details: Subcommands: ``html`` writes a swatch page, ``extract``/``extract-show`` gather the ``#rrggbb``/``rgb()`` colours of a tree (with ANSI previews), ``hex2rgb`` converts one value, ``showcolor`` prints random colour blocks and ``sorthue`` sorts the hex lines by hue.

compare_files_dirs.py.summary: File and directory comparison utilities in one CLI.
details: Subcommands: ``a-b`` prints the differing lines of two files, ``compare-dirs``/``compare-dirz`` report the hashes unique to each tree, ``fcmp``/``same-file`` compare two paths, ``pdif`` diffs the Python-aware content, ``pycommon`` finds the shared lines and ``compare-move`` moves or copies the common files.

compress_files_500k.py.summary: Compress the files above 500 KB below the current directory.
details: Streams each large file through xz (or the ``-b`` algorithm: gz, bz2, br, zst, lz4, 7z) in 1 MB chunks and replaces it with the archive; ``-d`` decompresses the recognised archives and ``--list``/``--show-reduction`` only the report the candidates.

compress_subdirs.py.summary: Compress or decompress the top-level directories of a folder in parallel.
details: Packs each subdirectory into a tar with xz, gz, bz2, zstd, lz4 or snappy (``-c``), or extracts the archives back (``-d``), with ``--min``/``--max`` size filters, ``--include`` globs, ``--keep``/``--remove-source`` handling and a choice of the multiprocessing or threading pool.

compresstools.py.summary: Compress or decompress files and folders with seven codecs.
details: Picks the algorithm with the flags (``-z`` zstd, ``-x`` xz, ``-7`` 7z, ``-g`` gzip, ``-b`` bz2, ``-r`` brotli, ``-l`` lz4), compresses the single files in memory or in chunks and the folders asynchronously, and ``-d`` decompresses the archives again.

compsub.py.summary: Compress the subdirectories of the current folder into tar.zst, tar.br or tar.xz.
details: Packs each directory with tar plus zstd (level 19), brotli (quality 11) or lzma, and ``-d`` safely extracts the archives again with a path-traversal guard; the algorithm, level and recursion depth are configurable.
